The final answer is incorrect. The error is in the triple-intersection term.

The event "no ace, no king, no queen" among the first $k$ cards means none of the $12$ cards of those three ranks appears. The remaining cards are $54-12=42$ (the $40$ standard cards of the other ranks plus the two jokers), not $2$. The proposed solution counted only the jokers and dropped the $40$ cards of the other ranks.

The corrected sum is

$$
\mathbb{E}[T]=3\sum_{k}\frac{\binom{50}{k}}{\binom{54}{k}}-3\sum_{k}\frac{\binom{46}{k}}{\binom{54}{k}}+\sum_{k}\frac{\binom{42}{k}}{\binom{54}{k}}.
$$

The identity $\sum_{k=0}^{a}\binom{a}{k}/\binom{N}{k}=\frac{N+1}{N+1-a}$ applies to each sum with $N=54$:

- $\sum_k \binom{50}{k}/\binom{54}{k} = 55/5 = 11$
- $\sum_k \binom{46}{k}/\binom{54}{k} = 55/9$
- $\sum_k \binom{42}{k}/\binom{54}{k} = 55/13$

Therefore

$$
\mathbb{E}[T]=33-\frac{55}{3}+\frac{55}{13}=\frac{44}{3}+\frac{55}{13}=\frac{572+165}{39}=\frac{737}{39}\approx 18.90.
$$

As a plausibility check, each rank's first appearance is the minimum of four positions, with expectation about $55/5=11$, and the time until all three ranks have appeared is the maximum of three such minima. A value near 19 fits this, whereas $2497/159\approx 15.7$ does not.

The correct answer is $\dfrac{737}{39}$, not $\dfrac{2497}{159}$.

VERDICT: REJECT
